chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ash'ari, from Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Azdi, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about Mut'ah (temporary marriage), is she from the four (permanent wives)? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No'.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu al-Hasan (Imam al-Rida, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْأَرْبَع: The four (referring to the four permanent wives allowed in Islam)

ai.seo_question: Is a wife in temporary marriage (Mut'ah) considered one of the four permanent wives in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the legal status of women in temporary marriage (Mut'ah) by explicitly negating their inclusion among the 'four' permanent wives mentioned in the Quran. This distinction is crucial in Shia jurisprudence for determining specific rights, such as inheritance and the requirement of exclusive cohabitation, which apply to permanent wives but not to Mut'ah spouses. The hadith underscores the unique contractual nature of Mut'ah, separating it from the permanent marital bond regulated by Surah An-Nisa.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Is’haq Al Ashary, from Bakr Bin Muhammad Al Azdy who said,
‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan about the Mut’a, is she from the four (allowable wives)?’ So heasws said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 2. AI-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ash’ariy from Bakr ibn Muhammad af-Azdiy who has said the following: “In response to my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about al-Mut‘ah (advantageous marriage) if it is one of the four, he (the Imam) said, ‘No, it is not one of the four.’”
